claims: The Artemis II crew will not land on the Moon.
The Artemis II crew will fly around the Moon.
The Artemis II spacecraft will splash down in the Pacific Ocean after a 10-day mission.
Artemis II serves as a test flight to validate life support systems and technology for future lunar landings.
Artemis II is a crewed mission to test the Orion spacecraft's systems in deep space.
The Artemis II crew will fly over the far side of the Moon at altitudes between 6,000 and 9,000 kilometers.
The Orion spacecraft is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean for recovery by U.S. Navy ships.
The Artemis II splashdown is planned for roughly 10 days after the April 1, 2026, launch.
The Artemis II launch is planned for April 1, 2026.
Artemis II marks the first crewed mission to the vicinity of the Moon since the Apollo era.
